title: SIG shared lexicon and copy system
about: P36.17 (K13 UXK14-4 / K14 §3.4–3.5, C-01…C-04). The ONE machine-readable vocabulary every surface reads — Astro components, the internal visual-language page, the map style and the Python figure kit (P36.27/28 read this file as plain JSON). One epistemic word means one thing everywhere (SIG-UI-143); one symbol carries one meaning (SIG-UI-133). Stored enums, JSON keys and spec terms are never rewritten — this file maps them to their display labels and plain-language meanings; the precise layer stays verbatim behind it (K14 §3.3).

resolution_status.label: Resolution
resolution_status.plain: The decision about which value the record currently stands on.

support.label: Support
support.plain: How strongly the winning value is evidenced.

agreement.label: Agreement
agreement.plain: How much the admissible evidence disagrees.

currency.label: Currency
currency.plain: How stale the claim is relative to how fast this kind of fact changes.

CONFIRMED.label: Confirmed
CONFIRMED.plain: The strongest backing SIG gives: the evidence settles this value.

STRONGLY_SUPPORTED.label: Strong support
STRONGLY_SUPPORTED.plain: Backed by one high-tier source or two mid-tier sources.

PROBABLE.label: Probable
PROBABLE.plain: Backed by a single mid-tier source.

WEAKLY_SUPPORTED.label: Weak support
WEAKLY_SUPPORTED.plain: Only thin evidence backs this value.

UNSUPPORTED.label: Unsupported
UNSUPPORTED.plain: No admissible claim backs this value; it is shown because something must be displayed.

UNCONTESTED.label: Uncontested
UNCONTESTED.plain: No admissible evidence disagrees with this value.

MINOR_DISAGREEMENT.label: Minor disagreement
MINOR_DISAGREEMENT.plain: Small differences within tolerance; no marker is raised.

CONTESTED.label: Contested
CONTESTED.plain: Sources disagree about this value; SIG shows the leading value and the others.

IRRECONCILABLE.label: Unresolved
IRRECONCILABLE.plain: Sources disagree and no value can be defended yet; see the range.

CURRENT.label: Current
CURRENT.plain: Fresh for this kind of fact.

AGING.label: Aging
AGING.plain: Getting old for this kind of fact.

STALE.label: Stale
STALE.plain: Older than this kind of fact should be; may have changed since.

HISTORICAL.label: Historical
HISTORICAL.plain: True at a past date, kept as history — shown with its date, e.g. 'Historical, recorded 2020-01-28', never 'undated'.

RESOLVED.label: Resolved
RESOLVED.plain: SIG has a recorded decision for this value.

UNRESOLVED.label: Unresolved
UNRESOLVED.plain: A legitimate, publishable outcome — not an error and never hidden.

WITHDRAWN.label: Withdrawn
WITHDRAWN.plain: Removed from publication; the reason is given.

PROVISIONAL.label: Provisional
PROVISIONAL.plain: Produced by a method not yet independently evaluated; may change.
PROVISIONAL.colourMeaning: amber means the provisional state only

UNREVIEWED.label: Not reviewed
UNREVIEWED.plain: No person outside the project has checked this.

NOT_REVIEWED_BY_PERSON.label: Not reviewed by a person
NOT_REVIEWED_BY_PERSON.plain: Produced by an automated step that no person has checked yet.

D1.label: Direct
D1.plain: This kind of document can show this kind of fact on its own.

D6.label: Not evidence
D6.plain: Non-probative for this predicate — excluded, not down-weighted.

CONFIGURED_ACCESS.label: Set up to share
CONFIGURED_ACCESS.plain: The system is set up to permit it — that says nothing about whether anyone used it.

DECLARED_POLICY.label: Stated policy
DECLARED_POLICY.plain: Someone said it is permitted or forbidden — distinct from configuration and from use.

NOT_RESEARCHED.label: Not researched
NOT_RESEARCHED.plain: SIG hasn't looked yet. Absence of a row is not evidence of absence.
NOT_RESEARCHED.symbolMeaning: absence kind, on the shared hatch

NO_EVIDENCE_FOUND.label: None found
NO_EVIDENCE_FOUND.plain: SIG searched the named sources and found nothing.
NO_EVIDENCE_FOUND.symbolMeaning: absence kind, on the shared hatch

EVIDENCE_OF_ABSENCE.label: Stated absent
EVIDENCE_OF_ABSENCE.plain: A source says this does not exist.
EVIDENCE_OF_ABSENCE.symbolMeaning: absence kind, on the shared hatch

UNRESOLVED.label: Unresolved
UNRESOLVED.plain: Evidence exists and disagrees; no resolution is defensible.
UNRESOLVED.symbolMeaning: absence kind, on the shared hatch

COPY.label: copy
COPY.plain: A second appearance of a record SIG already has — kept linked, counted once.

POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE.label: possible duplicate
POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE.plain: Possibly the same camera as another record. It stays visible and is not merged — SIG cannot prove they are the same, so counts are ranges.

INFERRED.label: Inferred
INFERRED.plain: Derived by a named rule from recorded claims — an L4 inference, not an observed fact. Its supporting claims are cited.

legend.note: The K13 C-01…C-04 collisions, resolved. One visual channel carries exactly one meaning; every encoding below is load-bearing and exclusive. Colour is never the only channel (SIG-UI-005).

corroborated.label: Corroborated
corroborated.plain: Two or more source records with independent lineages back this point or area.
corroborated.interimLegendLine: 2+ source records; republications not yet collapsed

singleSource.label: One source
singleSource.plain: One source record backs this point or area.

linePattern.meaning: access kind only — never currency, never a brand edge

currency.channel: muted ink plus a date or word
currency.plain: Staleness is shown as muted ink with a date or word ('Historical, recorded 2020-01-28'), never by a line pattern and never hollow.

contested.plain: Raspberry means contested or unresolved — nothing else.

provisional.channel: amber hue plus the ◔ outline or chip

absence.plain: Hatch means absence only; the four kinds are distinguished inside it.

entityKind.plain: Entity kind uses shape (point, area, institution, vendor) — shape never carries epistemic state.

cannotApply.label: Not applicable
cannotApply.plain: This measure does not apply to this fact — a typed state, never a blank cell.

dataHue.plain: Categorical data uses one hue plus shapes; the hue is the site's data blue.

candidateVsProvisional.note: Two different axes that must never collapse into each other (SIG-UI-062): Candidate is a lifecycle state (a record not yet committed); Provisional is an epistemic state (a method not yet evaluated). They differ in word, symbol and filter value.

rows.symbol: none — lifecycle states are filtered, not marked
rows.plain: A record that exists but is not yet part of the published record.
A published value produced by a method not yet independently evaluated.

vocabulary.concept: A place SIG publishes a page for
One source's row about a camera

terms.plain: A jurisdiction or named area SIG publishes a dossier for.
terms.example: Oklahoma City is a place; its dossier is the document SIG publishes about it.

terms.plain: The per-place document that gathers what SIG knows about that place's surveillance record.
terms.example: The Oklahoma City dossier lists the camera sites, the sharing edges and the gaps.

terms.plain: One source's row about a camera — what one document or dataset says about one thing.
terms.example: A procurement PDF's line naming a camera model is one record.

terms.plain: The de-duplicated physical camera — one real-world installation, possibly described by several records.
terms.example: Two vendor documents that describe the same pole camera are two records of one camera site.

terms.plain: Where SIG got something — the publisher and the document or dataset, named.
terms.example: The council minutes of 14 March are a source; so is the vendor's product page.

terms.plain: A dated published snapshot of the whole dataset — citable, immutable, never edited after the fact.
terms.example: Every page names the release it was built from in the footer.

terms.plain: One assertion, kept with its evidence and the raw words it came from — the substance of the graph.
terms.example: 'OKCPD operated 42 devices in 2020' is a claim backed by the auditor's report.

terms.plain: The immutable bytes SIG obtained at one instant — never edited; a redaction is a new capture.
terms.example: The PDF SIG fetched on 3 August is one capture; a later fetch of the same page is another.

terms.plain: The artifacts bearing on a claim — a claim never has just 'a source'.
terms.example: The evidence for the device count is the audit PDF plus the council minutes.

terms.plain: The system is set up to permit sharing — says nothing about whether anyone used it.
terms.example: An agency's platform is configured to share with the fusion centre.

terms.plain: Someone said sharing is permitted or forbidden — distinct from configuration and from use.
terms.example: A memorandum states the agency may share feeds with the state patrol.

terms.plain: Someone actually used the sharing — distinct from configured access and from declared policy.
terms.example: A query log shows a partner searched the camera list 41 times in June.

terms.plain: How directly this kind of document can show this kind of fact; a document can be strong evidence for one question and no evidence for another.
terms.example: A query log is direct evidence of use but no evidence of a written policy.

terms.plain: Produced by a method not yet independently evaluated; may change.
terms.example: The automated count of camera sites is provisional until the method's evaluation is published.

terms.plain: A record that exists but is not yet part of the published record — a lifecycle state, not an epistemic one.
terms.example: A camera site held back pending a rights review is a candidate.

terms.plain: The date the underlying data was taken — every figure and page names it.
terms.example: 'Data as of 27 Sep 2026' means nothing newer than that date is included.

terms.plain: The version of the rules that produced this value, shown in Technical details.
terms.example: A count produced under method v3 can differ from one under v2; the version is named.

terms.plain: How strongly the winning value is evidenced — one of the four fields, independent of agreement.
terms.example: 'Strong support' means one high-tier source, or two mid-tier sources, back the value.

terms.plain: How much the admissible evidence disagrees — one of the four fields, independent of support.
terms.example: A value can be strongly supported and still contested.

terms.plain: How stale a claim is relative to how fast this kind of fact changes — derived at query time, never stored.
terms.example: A camera count from 2020 is historical; a policy captured last month is current.

terms.plain: Sources disagree about this value; SIG shows the leading value and the others, marked ≠.
terms.example: '42 ≠' means one source says 42, another disagrees, and both are shown.

terms.plain: Evidence exists and disagrees, so no value can be defended — a legitimate published outcome, never hidden.
terms.example: Two credible sources give different counts and neither can be ruled out.

terms.plain: A second appearance of a record SIG already has — kept linked, counted once.
terms.example: The same camera appearing in two vendor catalogues is a copy, counted once.

terms.plain: Possibly the same camera as another record — kept visible and not merged, because SIG cannot prove they are the same.
terms.example: Two records 40 metres apart with the same model might be one camera; the count is shown as a range.

terms.plain: Backing from sources with independent lineages — republications of the same origin count once.
terms.example: A vendor page and the audit behind it are not independent; the audit and the council minutes are.

terms.plain: A review pass confirming a record's coordinates point at the place they claim.
terms.example: A location check caught a site pinned to the wrong side of the street.

terms.plain: The document or dataset that names what kind of machine a record describes.
terms.example: The procurement line naming the camera model is the technology source.

terms.plain: No person outside the project has checked this.
terms.example: An automated extraction marked 'Not reviewed' has had no human check yet.

terms.plain: A citation fixed to one immutable release, so the words cited still resolve after the next release.
terms.example: The 'Cite' action gives a URL that points at this exact snapshot.

terms.plain: The date a statement was true or the data was taken — always shown with its date.
terms.example: 'Data as of 27 Sep 2026' bounds what the figure can show.
